region: Cutchogue · North Fork of Long Island, New York
about: The Grapes of Roth is the personal label of Roman Roth, Wölffer Estate’s winemaker since 1992. Roth launched it in 2001 as a side project, and in 2013, when he became a partner at Wölffer, the label joined the estate’s portfolio as one of its premium wines. Roth helped found the Long Island Merlot Alliance and has long argued that Merlot, the island’s most widely planted red, is one of the great red grapes of the world.

Unlike most Wölffer wines, this Merlot comes from the North Fork, from fruit grown by Sam McCullough, a veteran Long Island vineyard manager whose McCullough Vineyard is in Cutchogue. The wine is made by Roth at Wölffer in Sagaponack; in earlier vintages it spent about 21 months in French oak barriques and was bottled unfined and unfiltered, a made-for-aging approach.

Wölffer’s notes for the 2020 describe a dark ruby wine with ripe cassis, plum, chocolate and hints of cinnamon and sandalwood, a rich, round palate with black pepper and olive tapenade, soft tannins, and a long finish of licorice, fig and toasted oak. The Beverage Testing Institute called it velvety smooth with a savory foundation made for the table.
facts: North Fork fruit from grower Sam McCullough (McCullough Vineyard, Cutchogue)
French oak barriques (about 21 months in past vintages)
